source_text: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τὴν ἐκείνων μετάνοιαν εἰς κοινὸν τοῦ βίου διδασκάλιον ὁ θεόπνευστος λόγος ἔγγραφον διέσωσεν. Ὁ πρεσβύτης ἐπ' ἐκείνων ἐθρήνει, καὶ τὴν πολιὰν ἔτιλλε καὶ διεσπάραττεν. Ὁ νεανίσκος, καὶ ἀκμά ζων, σφοδρότερον ἀπωδύρετο· ὁ πένης ἐστέναζεν· ὁ πλούσιος, ἐπιλαθόμενος τῆς τρυφῆς, ἤσκει τὴν κακοπάθειαν ὡς σώφρονα. Ὁ βασιλεὺς αὐτῶν τὴν λαμπρότητα καὶ τὴν δόξαν εἰς αἰσχύνην μετέβαλεν. Ἀπέθετο τὸν στέφανον, καὶ κόνιν τῆς κεφαλῆς κατεχέετο· τὴν ἁλουργίδα ῥίψας, σάκκον μετημφιάσατο· τὸν θρόνον τὸν ὑψηλὸν ἀφεὶς καὶ μετέωρον, ἐλεεινὸς τῇ γῇ προσεσύρετο· τὴν ἰδιάζουσαν καὶ βασιλικὴν καταλιπὼν εὐπάθειαν, συνεθρήνει τῷ δή μῳ· εἷς ἐγένετο τῶν πολλῶν, ὅτε τὸν κοινὸν πάντων Δεσπότην ἔβλεπεν ὀργιζόμενον. Τοῦτο δούλων εὐαισθήτων φρόνημα. Τοιαύτη τῶν ἁμαρτίαις ἐνεχομένων ἡ μετάνοια. Ἡμεῖς δὲ τὴν μὲν ἁμαρτίαν ἐπιτελοῦμεν συντόνως, ὀλιγώρως δὲ καὶ ῥᾳθύμως ἀναλαμβάνομεν τὴν μετάνοιαν. Τίς εὐξάμενος ἀποῤῥεῖ δάκρυον, ἵν' ὄμβρον λάβῃ καὶ σταγόνας εὐκαί ρους; Τίς ἐξαλείφων ἁμαρτίας, κατὰ μίμησιν τοῦ μακα ρίου Δαβὶδ, θρήνοις τὴν κοίτην ἔβρεξε; Τίς πόδας ἀπέπλυνε ξένων, καὶ τὴν κόνιν τῆς ὁδοιπορίας ἀπέκλυσεν, ἵν' ἐν καιρῷ δυσωπήσῃ τὸν Θεὸν, αὐχμοῦ λύσιν ζητῶν; Τίς ἔθρεψε τὸ πατρὸς ἔρημον παιδίον, ἵνα νῦν ἡμῖν ὁ Θεὸς θρέψῃ τὰ σιτία, ὡς ὀρφανὸν τῇ τῶν ἀνέμων ἀκρασίᾳ κονδυλιζόμενον; Τίς ἐθεράπευσε χήραν κεκακωμένην ταῖς δυσκολίαις τοῦ βίου, ἵνα νῦν ἐπιμετρηθῇ τὴν ἀναγκαίαν τροφήν; Διάῤῥηξον γραμματεῖον ἄδικον, ἵν' οὕτως ἡ ἁμαρτία λυθῇ. Ἐξ άλειψον βαρυτάτων τόκων ὁμολογίαν, ἵνα τέκῃ τὰ συν ήθη ἡ γῆ. Χαλκοῦ γὰρ καὶ χρυσοῦ καὶ τῶν ἀγόνων παρὰ φύσιν γεννώντων, ἡ κατὰ φύσιν τίκτουσα γίνεται στείρα, καὶ πρὸς τιμωρίαν τῶν ἐποικούντων κατεδικάσθη τὴν ἀκαρπίαν. Δειξάτωσαν τοίνυν οἱ τὴν πλεονεξίαν τιμῶντες, οἱ τὸν πλοῦτον μεθ' ὑπερβολῆς συνάγοντες, τίς ἡ δύναμις τῶν θησαυρισθέντων, ἢ τί τὸ ὄφελος, ἂν ὀργισθεὶς ὁ Θεὸς ἐπὶ πλεῖον παρελκύσῃ τὴν τιμωρίαν. Ὠχρότεροι τάχα τοῦ χρυσοῦ γενήσονται οἱ τοῦτον σωρεύοντες, ἐὰν μὴ τὸν ἄρτον, μέ χρι χθὲς καὶ πρώην καταφρονούμενον διὰ τὴν πρόχειρον ἐξουσίαν τῆς εὐθηνίας, σχῶσι. Δὸς δὴ μὴ εἶναι τὸν πιπράσκοντα, μηδὲ ὑπάρχειν σῖτον ἐν ἀπο θήκαις· καὶ τίς ἡ χρῆσις τῶν βαρυτάτων βαλαντίων; εἰπέ μοι. Οὐ μετ' ἐκείνων χωσθήσῃ; Οὐ γῆ ὁ χρυ σός; Οὐ πηλὸς ἀχρεῖος πηλῷ τῷ σώματι παρακείσε ται; Πάντα ἐκτήσω, καὶ ἓν ἀναγκαῖον οὐκ ἔχεις, δύναμιν τοῦ τρέφειν σεαυτόν. Τῷ παντί σου πλούτῳ ἓν νέφος ἀπέργασαι· ὀλίγων ψεκάδων ἐπινόησον πό ρον· ἔπειξον εἰς καρποφορίαν τὴν γῆν· λῦσον τῷ ὑπερηφάνῳ καὶ σοβοῦντι πλούτῳ τὴν συμφοράν. Τάχα τινὰ τῶν εὐλαβῶν παρακαλέσεις, ἵν' εὐχαῖς ὡς ὁ Θεσβίτης Ἠλίας ἄνεσίν σοι χαρίσηται τῶν δεινῶν, ἄνθρωπος ἀκτήμων, ὠχριῶν, ἀνυπόδετος, ἀοίκητος, ἀνέστιος, ἄπορος, ἑνὶ χιτῶνι σκεπόμενος, ὡς Ἠλίας τῇ μηλωτῇ, τὴν εὐχὴν ἔχων σύντροφον, τὴν ἐγκρά τειαν ὁμοδίαιτον. Κἂν ἐπιτύχῃς τῆς παρὰ τοῦ τοιού του βοηθείας δεόμενος, οὐ μακρὰ καταγελάσεις τῶν πολυμερίμνων κτημάτων; οὐ προσπτύσεις τῷ χρυσῷ; οὐ διαῤῥίψεις ὡς κόπρον τὸν ἄργυρον, ὃν πρότερον πάντα δυνάμενον καὶ φίλτατον ὀνομάζων, ἀδρανῆ βοηθὸν ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ἐγνώρισας; Διὰ σὲ καὶ τὴν συμφορὰν ταύτην κατεδίκασεν, ἐπειδὴ ἔχων οὐκ ἐδίδως· ἐπειδὴ παρέτρεχες τοὺς πεινῶντας· ἐπειδὴ πρὸς τοὺς ὀδυρομένους οὐκ ἐπεστρέφου· ἐπειδὴ προσκυνούμενος οὐκ ἠλέεις.
thought_title: The Ninevites' repentance as a model, and the uselessness of hoarded wealth in famine
orientation: Basil has just described the famine's devastation of the animals and now turns to the repentance of the Ninevites as a model for his hearers.
pass_a_gloss: And for this reason the God-inspired word preserved in writing their repentance as a common teaching for life. The old man among them was lamenting, and was plucking and tearing his gray hair. The young man, also in his prime, was wailing more violently; the poor man was groaning; the rich man, forgetting luxury, was practicing hardship as self-control. Their king changed his splendor and glory into shame. He laid aside the crown, and dust was being poured over his head; having thrown off the purple robe, he put on sackcloth; having left the high and lofty throne, he was dragging himself pitiable on the ground; having abandoned his private and royal comfort, he was lamenting together with the people; he became one of the many, when he saw the common Master of all being angry. This is the mindset of sensitive servants. Such is the repentance of those held in sins. But we complete the sin intensely, and carelessly and idly we take up the repentance. Who praying lets fall a tear, in order that he may receive rain and timely drops? Who wiping away sins, in imitation of the blessed David, wet his bed with laments? Who washed the feet of strangers, and washed away the dust of the journey, in order that in time he may appease God, seeking release from drought? Who fed the fatherless child of a father, in order that now God may nourish the crops for us, as an orphan being beaten by the intemperance of the winds? Who cared for a widow afflicted by the hardships of life, in order that now the necessary food may be measured out to him? Tear up the unjust contract, in order that thus the sin may be dissolved. Wipe out the agreement of very heavy interest, in order that the earth may give birth to its usual produce. For because of bronze and gold and of the things that unnaturally give birth to barren things, the earth that gives birth according to nature becomes barren, and was condemned to unfruitfulness for the punishment of those dwelling on it. Let those honoring greed show then, those gathering wealth with excess, what is the power of the hoarded things, or what is the benefit, if God being angry prolongs the punishment further. Paler perhaps than gold will those heaping it up become, if they do not have bread, until yesterday and the day before despised because of the ready abundance of plenty. Grant indeed that there is no seller, and that there is no grain in storehouses; and what is the use of the very heavy money-bags? tell me. Will you not be buried with them? Is not gold earth? Will not useless clay lie beside clay, the body? You acquired all things, and one necessary thing you do not have, the power to feed yourself. With all your wealth you have produced one cloud; devise a means for a few drops; press the earth to fruitfulness; release the disaster by your arrogant and swaggering wealth. Perhaps you will call upon one of the pious, in order that by prayers as Elijah the Tishbite he may grant you relief from the terrible things, a man without possessions, pale, barefoot, homeless, hearthless, resourceless, covered with one tunic, as Elijah with the sheepskin, having prayer as his companion, self-control as his housemate. And if you obtain the help from such a man by asking, will you not soon laugh at the many-cared-for possessions? will you not spit upon the gold? will you not throw away as dung the silver, which formerly you called all-powerful and dearest, but recognized as a weak helper in time of need? Because of you he condemned also this disaster, since having you did not give; since you were passing by the hungry; since you did not turn toward those lamenting; since being worshipped you did not have mercy.

pass_b_english: And for this reason the God-inspired word preserved their repentance in writing as a common teaching for life. The old man among them mourned, and tore and scattered his gray hair. The young man, in his prime, wailed all the more violently. The poor man groaned. The rich man, forgetting his luxury, practiced hardship like a man of self-control. Their king turned his splendor and glory into shame. He laid aside his crown and poured dust over his head. He threw off his purple robe and put on sackcloth instead. He left his high and lofty throne and was dragged pitiably along the ground. Abandoning his private royal comfort, he mourned together with the people. He became one of the many when he saw the common Master of all angry. This is the mindset of sensitive servants. Such is the repentance of those entangled in sins. But we carry out sin intensely, and carelessly and idly we take up the repentance. Who has prayed and shed a tear, so as to receive rain and timely drops? Who, wiping away sins in imitation of the blessed David, has wet his bed with lamentations? Who has washed the feet of strangers and rinsed off the dust of their journey, so as to move God at the right time, seeking release from the drought? Who has fed a child bereft of its father, so that now God may feed our crops, which are being battered like an orphan by the violence of the winds? Who has cared for a widow afflicted by the hardships of life, so that now the necessary food may be measured out to us? Tear up the unjust contract, so that in this way the sin may be dissolved. Erase the record of the heaviest interest, so that the earth may give birth to its usual produce. For while bronze and gold, things sterile by nature, are producing unnaturally, the earth that gives birth according to nature becomes barren, and has been condemned to fruitlessness for the punishment of its inhabitants. Let those who honor greed, then, those who gather wealth to excess, show what the power of their hoarded things is, or what the benefit is, if God in anger prolongs the punishment further. Those who heap up gold will perhaps become paler than the gold itself, unless they have bread—the bread that until yesterday and the day before was despised because of the ready abundance at hand. Suppose there is no one selling, and no grain in the storehouses: what is the use of the most oppressive money-bags? Tell me. Will you not be buried with them? Is not gold earth? Will not useless clay lie beside clay, the body? You acquired everything, and you do not have the one necessary thing: the power to feed yourself. With all your wealth you have not produced a single cloud. Devise a channel for a few drops. Urge the earth to bear fruit. Loose the disaster from your proud and swaggering wealth. Perhaps you will call upon one of the devout, so that by his prayers, like Elijah the Tishbite, he may grant you relief from these terrors—a man without possessions, pale, barefoot, without house, without hearth, without resources, covered by a single tunic, as Elijah was by his sheepskin, having prayer as his constant companion and self-control as his housemate. And if you obtain help from such a man when you ask, will you not soon laugh at your many-cared-for possessions? Will you not spit upon gold? Will you not throw away silver like dung—silver which you formerly called all-powerful and dearest, but which you have now recognized as a helpless ally in time of need? For your sake he also condemned this disaster, since you had and did not give; since you passed by the hungry; since you did not turn toward those who were weeping; since you were honored and did not show mercy.

problems.quote: he may be given in measure the necessary food
problems.source_quote: ἵνα νῦν ἐπιμετρηθῇ τὴν ἀναγκαίαν τροφήν
problems.why: Subject shifts to 'he' but ἐπιμετρηθῇ is passive; 'he may be given' obscures that God gives food to the widow's helper, not the widow.
problems.fix: so that now the necessary food may be measured out to you

problems.quote: while bronze and gold and the things that unnaturally give birth are producing
problems.source_quote: Χαλκοῦ γὰρ καὶ χρυσοῦ καὶ τῶν ἀγόνων παρὰ φύσιν γεννώντων
problems.why: ἀγόνων means 'sterile/barren,' not 'things that give birth'—the contrast is between sterile things unnaturally producing and fertile earth becoming barren.
problems.fix: For while bronze and gold, things sterile by nature, are producing unnaturally

problems.quote: Blot out the agreement of the heaviest interest
problems.why: 'ἐξάλειψον' = blot out/erase (a debt record), not 'blot out the agreement.' The point is cancelling a debt of heavy interest.
problems.fix: Erase the record of the heaviest interest
problems.ruling: 'Agreement' misrepresents ὁμολογίαν as contract rather than debt acknowledgment/record.

problems.quote: He condemned this disaster as well
problems.source_quote: Διὰ σὲ καὶ τὴν συμφορὰν ταύτην κατεδίκασεν
problems.why: Subject is God, not 'He' ambiguous; 'condemned this disaster' wrong agency—God condemned the land to barrenness, not the disaster itself.
problems.fix: For your sake God condemned the land to this disaster as well
problems.ruling: κατεδίκασεν takes τὴν ἀκαρπίαν as object earlier; here God condemned the land to this disaster, not 'condemned the disaster itself.'

edits.new: so that now the necessary food may be measured out to you

edits.old: For while bronze and gold and the things that unnaturally give birth are producing, the earth that gives birth according to nature becomes barren
edits.new: For while bronze and gold, things sterile by nature, are producing unnaturally, the earth that gives birth according to nature becomes barren

edits.old: Because of you He condemned this disaster as well

fixed: Changed 'he may be given in measure' to 'the necessary food may be measured out to you' to reflect the passive voice and the implied divine agent.
Changed 'the things that unnaturally give birth are producing' to 'things sterile by nature, are producing unnaturally' to correctly render ἀγόνων as 'sterile/barren.'
Changed 'Blot out the agreement' to 'Erase the record' to reflect the sense of cancelling a debt record.
Changed 'He condemned this disaster' to 'God condemned the land to this disaster' to clarify the subject and the object of condemnation.

problems.quote: the necessary food may be measured out to you
problems.source_quote: ἵνα νῦν ἐπιμετρηθῇ τὴν ἀναγκαίαν τροφήν
problems.why: ἡμῖν (to us) is implied by context, not 'to you'; also passive 'may be measured out' obscures divine subject.
problems.fix: so that now the necessary food may be measured out to us

problems.quote: was dragging himself pitiable on the ground
problems.why: προσεσύρετο is passive or middle, 'was dragged,' not active 'dragging himself.'
problems.fix: was dragged pitiably along the ground
problems.ruling: προσεσύρετο is middle/passive; 'was dragged' not 'dragging himself.' Subject is ἐλεεινὸς, pitiable.

problems.quote: Release the disaster by means of your proud and swaggering wealth
problems.source_quote: λῦσον τῷ ὑπερηφάνῳ καὶ σοβοῦντι πλούτῳ τὴν συμφοράν
problems.why: λῦσον is imperative 'loose/release [the disaster] from,' not 'release by means of'; dative is disadvantage, not instrument.
problems.fix: Loose the disaster from your proud and swaggering wealth
problems.ruling: λῦσον τῷ πλούτῳ τὴν συμφοράν: dative is separation/disadvantage, 'release the disaster FROM wealth,' not 'by means of.'

problems.quote: For your sake God condemned the land to this disaster as well
problems.source_quote: Διὰ σὲ καὶ τὴν συμφορὰν ταύτην κατεδίκασεν
problems.why: κατεδίκασεν has no explicit subject; context suggests God, but 'the land' is object of τὴν συμφοράν, not 'condemned the land.'
problems.fix: For your sake he condemned [us] to this disaster as well
problems.ruling: τὴν συμφορὰν ταύτην = 'this disaster' is direct object of κατεδίκασεν. No 'land' in source; 'condemned the land' adds unsupported word.

edits.old: so that now the necessary food may be measured out to you
edits.new: so that now the necessary food may be measured out to us

edits.old: was dragging himself pitiable on the ground
edits.new: was dragged pitiably along the ground

edits.old: Release the disaster by means of your proud and swaggering wealth
edits.new: Loose the disaster from your proud and swaggering wealth

edits.old: For your sake God condemned the land to this disaster as well
edits.new: For your sake he condemned us to this disaster as well

fixed: Changed 'to you' to 'to us' to match implied ἡμῖν in context.
Changed 'was dragging himself' to 'was dragged' to reflect passive/middle προσεσύρετο.
Changed 'Release the disaster by means of' to 'Loose the disaster from' to reflect dative of disadvantage.
Changed 'God condemned the land' to 'he condemned us' to reflect that κατεδίκασεν has no explicit subject and 'the land' is not the object.

problems.why: 'heaviest' is wrong sense of βαρυτάτων here; means 'most oppressive/burdensome' money-bags, not weighty.

problems.quote: For your sake he condemned us to this disaster as well
problems.source_quote: Διὰ σὲ καὶ τὴν συμφορὰν ταύτην κατεδίκασεν
problems.why: Subject is God, not 'he'; 'us' wrong: God condemned this disaster, not 'us to disaster'.
problems.fix: For your sake he also condemned this disaster
problems.ruling: κατεδίκασεν has no explicit subject; context shows God is subject, and 'us' is unsupported—God condemned the disaster itself, not 'us'.

problems.why: 'as self-control' misreads σώφρονα (temperate/chaste person, predicate noun); he practiced hardship like a temperate man.
problems.fix: practiced hardship like a man of self-control
problems.ruling: σώφρονα is predicate noun ('as a temperate man'), not adverbial 'as self-control'; changes meaning.

edits.old: For your sake he condemned us to this disaster as well
edits.new: For your sake he also condemned this disaster
practiced hardship like a man of self-control

fixed: Changed 'heaviest money-bags' to 'most oppressive money-bags': βαρυτάτων here means burdensome/oppressive, not physically heavy.
Changed 'For your sake he condemned us to this disaster as well' to 'For your sake he also condemned this disaster': the subject is God, and the object is the disaster, not 'us'.
Changed 'was practicing hardship as self-control' to 'practiced hardship like a man of self-control': σώφρονα is a predicate noun meaning temperate person, not the abstract noun self-control.

refereed.quote: loose the disaster from your proud and swaggering wealth
refereed.source_quote: λῦσον τῷ ὑπερηφάνῳ καὶ σοβοῦντι πλούτῳ τὴν συμφοράν
refereed.why: λῦσον = 'loose/release' but object is 'the disaster'; syntax twisted. 'Loose the disaster from' is unclear.
refereed.fix: release the disaster from your proud and swaggering wealth
refereed.ruling: 'Loose the disaster from wealth' is awkward; λῦσον τὴν συμφορὰν means 'release/avert the disaster from' wealth.
